saa-ini-013.text: A company hired a consulting firm that owns its own account AWS. Consulting needs to access specific resources in the company's account, without user creation IAM The European Commission has been working on a proposal for a Council Directive on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States relating to the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to the IAM allows this access between accounts safely?
options: Create a IAM Role in the company account that can be assumed by the users of the consulting account
Create a user IAM with password for each consultant in the company account
Making public the resources the consultancy needs to access
Share the company administrator's access keys with the consulting
saa-ini-013.explanation: Roles between accounts (cross-account roles) allow identities from another account to temporarily assume a set of defined permissions, without creating permanent credentials — the recommended way of granting access between accounts.
saa-ini-013.hint: Think about the resource of IAM which may be temporarily 'absorbed' by identities of another account.
optionRationales: Roles between accounts (cross-account roles) allow identities from another account to temporarily assume a set of defined permissions, without creating permanent credentials — the recommended way of granting access between accounts.
Sharing credentials is a serious security breach: keys are long-term, unauditable per person and give wide access without control.
Creating permanent users runs counter to the scenario requirement and increases the attack surface, requiring management of external credentials.
Exposing resources publicly to solve a problem of punctual access would open the data to the whole internet — the opposite of a secure solution.

saa-ini-014.text: A company already has a corporate directory (such as Microsoft Active Directory) with all its employees. AWS using your existing corporate credentials, without needing to create a user IAM for each. As this objective is called and enabled in the AWS?
options: Creation of permanent key accesses for each employee
Sharing of root credentials between departments
Identity Federation, allowing authenticated users in the corporate directory to assume roles in AWS
User replication, automatically copying each AD account to the IAM
saa-ini-014.explanation: The identity federation integrates an external identity provider (such as the AD) to AWS: the user authenticates in the corporate directory and receives temporary credentials via roles, eliminating the duplication of users in the IAM.
saa-ini-014.hint: The key concept is to trust the authentication done by an external identity provider — what is called?
optionRationales: The identity federation integrates an external identity provider (such as the AD) to AWS: the user authenticates in the corporate directory and receives temporary credentials via roles, eliminating the duplication of users in the IAM.
There is no recommended mechanism for copying AD users to the IAM; the correct approach is to federate authentication, keeping the identities only in the directory of origin..
Root credentials should never be shared or used on a daily basis — this practice is unrelated to corporate directory integration.
Permanent access keys for each employee is precisely the scenario that the federation avoids, reducing risks and work of managing credentials.

saa-ini-015.text: An organization owns 15 accounts AWS and wants its employees to log in once on a central portal and, from it, access all accounts and applications allowed, without managing users IAM separate in each account. AWS provides this unique login experience (SSO)?
saa-ini-015.explanation: The IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) centralizes staff access to multiple accounts AWS and applications in a single login portal, with centrally managed permissions.
saa-ini-015.hint: Think of the service whose name unites 'identity' and 'centre': the central point of the workforce's login.
optionRationales: The IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) centralizes staff access to multiple accounts AWS and applications in a single login portal, with centrally managed permissions.
The Cognito manage user authentication FINAIS of web and mobile applications (clients), and not the access of employees to multiple accounts AWS.
The Secrets Manager store and rotate application secrets (signs, tokens), without any unique login portal function for accounts AWS.
The ACM issue and renew certificates TLS/SSL for cryptography in transit, does not manage logins or access to accounts.

saa-ini-016.text: A startup is building a mobile app and needs a managed service to take care of the registration, login and password recovery of the end users of the app, with support for social login (Google, Facebook) and integration with protected APIs. AWS meets this need?
saa-ini-016.explanation: The Cognito provides registration, authentication and end-user management for web and mobile applications (user pools), including social login and token issuance for secure API access.
saa-ini-016.hint: Differentiate who makes login: employees at AWS (IAM/Identity Center) versus clients of your application (which service?).
optionRationales: The Cognito provides registration, authentication and end-user management for web and mobile applications (user pools), including social login and token issuance for secure API access.
The IAM manage identities and permissions to access resources from AWS (administrators, developers, services), and no end-customer accounts of an application.
The Identity Center centralizes labour force access to accounts AWS and corporate applications, not the login of millions of end users of an app.
Directory Service provides Active Directory managed for Windows corporate scenarios, not authentication of mobile app clients with social login.

saa-ini-017.text: In a multi-account architecture with AWS Organizations, the governance team has applied a policy that prevents all accounts of the organizational unit 'Development' from excluding tracks from CloudTrail, regardless of permissions IAM What kind of policy does this control?
saa-ini-017.explanation: SCPs are applied at the level of the organization (root, OOs or accounts) and define the maximum limit of permissions: actions denied by the SCP are blocked even for administrators with full access via IAM.
saa-ini-017.hint: It is the 'guarda-chuva' policy of the Organizations that even the account administrator can't get around.
optionRationales: SCPs are applied at the level of the organization (root, OOs or accounts) and define the maximum limit of permissions: actions denied by the SCP are blocked even for administrators with full access via IAM.
Policies IAM act within a single account and can be changed by local administrators — do not impose an inviolable organizational limit on all accounts.
Bucket police control access to a specific Bucket S3, without the ability to restrict actions on the CloudTrail in multiple accounts.
NACLs filter network traffic in sub-networks and are not related to API or account governance.

saa-ini-018.text: Courts EC2 in private sub-networks need to access the Amazon S3 and the DynamoDB without the traffic passing through the public internet and without using NAT Gateway. What's the use of VPC creates this private path for these two services, without additional cost?
saa-ini-018.explanation: Gateway Endpoints are offered specifically for S3 and DynamoDB: add a private route in the route table of the VPC, allowing access to these services through the internal network of the AWS, without internet, without NAT and no cost.
saa-ini-018.hint: There are two services AWS which have gained a special type of 'gateway' endpoint, free, configured in the route table.
optionRationales: Gateway Endpoints are offered specifically for S3 and DynamoDB: add a private route in the route table of the VPC, allowing access to these services through the internal network of the AWS, without internet, without NAT and no cost.
The Internet Gateway provides just access to the public internet — the opposite of the private path desired for private sub-networks.
The peering connects two VPCs to each other, but does not create a private path between a VPC and regional services such as S3 and DynamoDB.
The NAT Gateway would route traffic to the public internet at a cost per hour and per GB — the scenario asks exactly to eliminate this dependence.

saa-ini-019.text: A software company wants to expose its service hosted at AWS for customers to consume privately, directly from their VPCs, without the traffic crossing the public internet and without creating peering between networks. AWS enables this private exposure of services between VPCs?
options: Internet Gateway with restrictive rules Security Group
AWS Direct Connect among the customers' VPCs
saa-ini-019.explanation: PrivateLink allows you to post a service behind a Network Load Balancer and consume it from other VPCs by means of endpoints interface with private IPs, keeping all traffic within the network of AWS no peering or internet.
saa-ini-019.hint: Think of the 'private link' that turns your service into an endpoint within the VPC of the customer.
optionRationales: PrivateLink allows you to post a service behind a Network Load Balancer and consume it from other VPCs by means of endpoints interface with private IPs, keeping all traffic within the network of AWS no peering or internet.
Even with restrictive rules, traffic would cross the public internet — what the scenario wants to avoid altogether.
The Direct Connect link data centers on-premises to AWS; is not the mechanism for private consumption of services between cloud VPCs.
The CloudFront content delivery on the edge of the public internet; geographical restrictions do not make the private path within the AWS.

saa-ini-020.text: An architect created a new Security Group in one VPC and attached it to a court EC2 without adding any rules. What is the standard behavior of this Security Group newly created?
options: All incoming traffic is denied and all outgoing traffic is allowed
All inbound and outbound traffic allowed
Only traffic SSH (door 22) is allowed at the entrance
All incoming and outgoing traffic is denied
saa-ini-020.explanation: By default, a Security Group new has no entry rules (logo, implicitly denies all entry traffic) and has a rule releasing all exit traffic.
saa-ini-020.hint: Remember the standard posture: closed doors for those who arrive, free passage for those who leave.
optionRationales: By default, a Security Group new has no entry rules (logo, implicitly denies all entry traffic) and has a rule releasing all exit traffic.
If everything was allowed by default, newly created instances would be exposed; the entry starts completely blocked until Allow rules are added.
The output is released by default to allow the instance to start connections (updates, APIs); only the input starts blocked.
No input door is automatically released — not even SSH; the administrator needs to explicitly create each entry rule.

saa-ini-021.text: Administrators need access via SSH cases EC2 which are in private sub-networks, without exposing these instances directly to the internet. A traditional practice is to place a reinforced intermediate instance in a public sub-network, which serves as the only entry point to reach private instances. As this component is called?
saa-ini-021.explanation: The bastion host is a hardened instance in the public sub-network that concentrates and controls administrative access (SSH/RDP) to private sub-networks, reducing the area exposed to the internet.
saa-ini-021.hint: The name comes from the fortifications: the reinforced tower where everyone must pass to enter the castle.
optionRationales: The bastion host is a hardened instance in the public sub-network that concentrates and controls administrative access (SSH/RDP) to private sub-networks, reducing the area exposed to the internet.
The NAT Gateway allows private bodies INICIEM exit connections to the internet; it does not accept administrative entry connections as SSH.
The Internet Gateway is the routing component that connects the VPC internet — is not a controlled administrative access body.
The ELB distributes application traffic between instances, not administrative sessions SSH for private server management.

saa-ini-022.text: Courts EC2 in a private sub-network need to download internet security updates, but can not, under any circumstances, receive connections started from outside. Which component meets this exit requirement without allowing entry into the network.?
options: Internet Gateway directly attached to the private sub-network with public IPs in the fora
VPC Peering with a VPC public
NAT Gateway in a public sub-network, referenced in the route table of the private sub-network
saa-ini-022.explanation: The NAT Gateway allows private instances to start output connections to the internet (such as downloading patches) while blocking externally initiated connections, preserving sub-network isolation.
saa-ini-022.hint: Think of the component that works as 'one-handed swivel door': inside you can exit, outside you can't enter.
optionRationales: The NAT Gateway allows private instances to start output connections to the internet (such as downloading patches) while blocking externally initiated connections, preserving sub-network isolation.
Assign public IPs and route to Internet Gateway would make the instances reachable from the internet — decharacterizing the private subnet and violating the requirement.
Peering connects VPCs to each other; it does not provide translation of addresses to controlled output to the internet.
The WAF filter web requests that reach CloudFront, ALB or API Gateway; does not provide way out to the internet from private sub-networks.

saa-ini-023.text: A company needs to quickly connect its office to its VPC the AWS with encrypted traffic, using the internet as a means of transport and IPsec tunnels, without waiting for the installation of physical circuits. What hybrid connectivity solution meets this scenario?
saa-ini-023.explanation: The Site-to-Site VPN establishes encrypted IPsec tunnels between the company's local gateway and the VPC through the internet, it can be provided in hours — ideal when speed and encryption are the priorities.
saa-ini-023.hint: The combination 'internet + IPsec tunnel + activation speed' describes the classic encrypted connectivity option.
optionRationales: The Site-to-Site VPN establishes encrypted IPsec tunnels between the company's local gateway and the VPC through the internet, it can be provided in hours — ideal when speed and encryption are the priorities.
The Direct Connect uses dedicated physical circuits that take weeks to provide; it offers consistent band, but does not meet the requirement of fast deployment via internet.
The peering connects two VPCs inside the AWS, and not an on-premises office to a VPC.
The Route 53 solve names DNS; does not establish encrypted network tunnels between environments.

saa-ini-024.text: No. AWS KMS, a team evaluates using keys managed by AWS or customer-managed keys (customer managed keys). What is the main advantage of choosing a customer-managed key?
options: They are totally free, unlike keys managed by AWS
They're the only ones who can encrypt data on S3
Eliminate the need for permissions IAM for key use
Total control over key policy, rotation, enable/disable and who can use it
saa-ini-024.explanation: Client-managed keys give complete administrative control: defining key policies, managing rotation, disabling and scheduled exclusion — necessary for rigid governance and audit requirements.
saa-ini-024.hint: The central difference is who runs the key: think about politics, rotation and life cycle under your command.
optionRationales: Client-managed keys give complete administrative control: defining key policies, managing rotation, disabling and scheduled exclusion — necessary for rigid governance and audit requirements.
It's the opposite: customer-managed keys have monthly cost per key, while those managed by AWS do not generate direct storage charge.
The S3 can use both keys managed by AWS the customer (and SSE-S3); cryptography is not exclusive to a type of key.
The use of any key KMS remains subject to permissions (key policies and IAM); access control is never eliminated.
